entries.design: three-phase experiment: learning phase (6 cases) under structured reflection vs immediate diagnosis vs differential diagnosis; immediate and 1-week delayed tests with new cases of the same diseases
entries.population: 46 Year-4 medical students (Brazil)
entries.operation: diagnostic_reasoning: diagnosing written clinical cases
entries.comparator: immediate single diagnosis; listing a differential diagnosis

outcome.measure: diagnostic accuracy (0-1) on new cases of studied diseases

estimate.value: Immediate: reflection 0.48 [0.38, 0.58] < differential 0.62 [0.54, 0.70]; 1 week: reflection 0.66 [0.56, 0.76] > differential 0.48 [0.37, 0.58] and immediate 0.52 [0.43, 0.60]
estimate.note: Reflection disadvantage immediately, advantage after a week; generating a differential alone did not help delayed learning.

entries.bias_and_applicability: Small sample, one site, developer group; written vignettes; same diseases at test (near transfer only). Key design lesson: immediate performance would have ranked the conditions the wrong way round.

entries.bias_and_applicability: Single study, written cases; far transfer to adjacent diseases absent in all groups - reflection practice does not substitute for disease knowledge.

entries.intervention: CFS training as recommended by experts

entries.design: web-based vignette study, 4 validated cases (2 easier, 2 harder) in 4 sequential phases, confidence after each phase
entries.population: 118 US general internists from an online physician community
entries.operation: diagnostic_reasoning + self_regulation: calibration of confidence

estimate.value: Accuracy 55.3% (easier) vs 5.8% (harder); confidence 7.2 vs 6.4 of 10
estimate.note: Higher confidence associated with fewer requests for additional tests (p = .01).

entries.bias_and_applicability: Volunteer online sample, vignettes; practising physicians, not students. Shows confidence is insensitive to accuracy in hard cases: self-rated certainty cannot gate competence claims and should be captured and compared with outcomes (calibration feedback), not trusted.

entries.operation: diagnostic_reasoning + procedural skills: virtual patient cases
entries.comparator: traditional education; blended; other digital education

sections_read: Methods: structured-reflection scoring rubric, blinded scorers

entries.design: single-blind RCT (NCT06157944), 60 min for up to 6 vignettes, stratified by career stage
entries.population: 50 US physicians (26 attendings, 24 residents) in family, internal, emergency medicine
entries.operation: diagnostic_reasoning: differential diagnosis with supporting/opposing findings and next steps
entries.comparator: conventional resources only; exploratory LLM-alone arm

outcome.measure: structured-reflection rubric score (%) graded by blinded experts

estimate.value: LLM-assisted 76% vs conventional 74% median; adjusted difference 2 pp [-4, 8], p = .60; LLM alone +16 pp [2, 30] vs conventional
estimate.note: Rubric reliability: weighted kappa 0.66 across 3 graders; Cronbach alpha 0.64.

entries.bias_and_applicability: Small trial, vignettes, single model version (2023), no prompt training. Two R3-relevant points: access to a strong model did not improve human reasoning scores; and grading of differential-diagnosis reasoning reached only moderate reliability even with expert rubric (kappa 0.66).
